metadata.title: Bullion Sales Tax in Alaska (2026): Rules, Exemptions & Examples

description: Alaska has 0% statewide sales tax. Bullion isn’t taxed by the state, but some municipalities tax delivered sales. Check local rules at checkout.

What's covered by the exemption
Alaska has no state sales tax, so there is no state-level exemption to apply. Some local jurisdictions may still tax.
How they decide what counts as bullion
No state-level decision to make. Your delivery address determines whether a local borough or city collects.
What's NOT covered
Local city/borough code controls
Even when the state-level rule is clear, cities or counties in this state may charge their own tax. Here's what to expect.
Local treatment
Use ARSSTC/local jurisdiction rules
Common questions about sales tax on gold and silver in Alaska.
Is gold bullion taxed in Alaska?
+
There is no Alaska state sales tax, so the state does not tax gold bullion. Local municipality rules may still apply to delivered sales.
Do I owe sales tax on silver coins shipped to Alaska?
+
Not at the state level because Alaska has no statewide sales tax. Any tax due depends on the destination municipality’s local sales-tax rules.
Are numismatic coins taxable in Alaska?
+
Alaska does not impose state sales tax on numismatic coins, but local sales taxes can differ by jurisdiction. Review the local rules where the order is delivered.
Does Alaska have a bullion exemption threshold?
+
No statewide threshold is needed because Alaska has no state sales tax. Local jurisdictions may have their own rules and definitions.
